definition: The L2 norm is the Euclidean norm, which represents the length of a vector in Euclidean space, calculated from the square root of the sum of the squared vector components.
details: The L2 norm is the Euclidean norm, which represents the length of a vector in Euclidean space, calculated from the square root of the sum of the squared vector components.

explainer.lead: The L2 norm is the Euclidean norm, the length of a vector in Euclidean space. It is a basic measure of vector magnitude used throughout machine learning.

tiers.eli5: It's just the straight-line length of an arrow, found by squaring each part, adding them up, and taking the square root.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers compute it to measure vector magnitude, such as normalizing embeddings or checking gradient size. A pitfall is that squaring large components makes it sensitive to outliers.
tiers.paperLevel: For a vector, the L2 norm is the square root of the sum of its squared components. It is not robust to large individual components because they are squared.

explainer.example: The vector (3, 4) has L2 norm equal to the square root of 9 plus 16, which is 5.
